questions.q: What problem does Slim CI solve, according to this lesson?
options: A CI run rebuilding an entire large project on every PR, even when only one model actually changed
dbt projects being too small to need CI at all
Git branches conflicting with each other
Production schemas being visible to developers
questions.explain: Without Slim CI, dbt build on a PR rebuilds the whole project by default — slow and wasteful when only one model changed.

questions.q: What does the `state:modified+` selector actually select?
options: Resources that differ from a comparison manifest, plus everything downstream of each modified resource
Every single model in the project, with no filtering
Only models that have never been run before
Only tests, never models
questions.explain: state:modified finds what changed versus a prior manifest; the trailing + extends that to downstream dependents too.

questions.q: Why is deferral (`--defer`) necessary in addition to `state:modified+`?
options: Because a downstream model's ref() still needs to resolve to something, even for upstream models this partial run didn't rebuild
Deferral is optional decoration with no functional purpose
Deferral replaces the need for state:modified+ entirely
Deferral only affects which Git branch is checked out
questions.explain: Deferral resolves ref() calls for unselected models against a prior run (e.g. production) instead of requiring them to exist in the current partial run.

questions.q: In the real dbt Cloud CI run shown in this lesson, what did 'executed in deferred mode' mean?
options: The run used a manifest from a prior production run as its comparison/resolution point
The run was postponed indefinitely and never executed
The run ignored all Git branches
The run deleted the production environment
questions.explain: The run record explicitly stated it executed in deferred mode using a manifest from a specific prior production run.

questions.q: Does a dbt Cloud CI job require you to manually write the `--state` path yourself?
options: No — once Slim CI is enabled, dbt Cloud already knows the last successful production run's manifest to compare against
Yes, it must be typed into the job's YAML by hand every time
Yes, but only on the first run ever
state:modified+ cannot be used inside dbt Cloud at all
questions.explain: dbt Cloud's CI job applies state:modified+ and deferral automatically against its known prior production state — no manual --state path needed.
